youtube.aciklama:
How do we measure how much tinnitus affects a person's life? In this lesson we cover the structure, scoring and five-grade interpretation of the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory (THI), the eight subscales of the Tinnitus Functional Index (TFI), criteria for meaningful change, and the use of these questionnaires in diagnosis and follow-up.

AIHEAR Audiology Academy makes short, clear lessons for audiology students and professionals.

Sources: Newman, Jacobson and Spitzer, Development of the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, Arch Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg (1996); Newman, Sandridge and Jacobson, Psychometric adequacy of the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, J Am Acad Audiol (1998); Zeman et al., Tinnitus Handicap Inventory for evaluating treatment effects: which changes are clinically relevant?, Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery (2011); McCombe et al., Guidelines for the grading of tinnitus severity, Clinical Otolaryngology (2001); Meikle et al., The Tinnitus Functional Index, Ear and Hearing (2012); Aksoy, Fırat and Alpar, The Tinnitus Handicap Inventory: a study of validity and reliability, International Tinnitus Journal (2007); Tunkel et al., Clinical Practice Guideline: Tinnitus (2014); NICE NG155 (2020).

This video is for educational purposes and does not replace diagnosis or treatment.

cumleler: Hello, and welcome to the AIHEAR Audiology Academy.
In this lesson we will learn two common scales of tinnitus impact: the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory and the Tinnitus Functional Index.
We will cover the structure of the scales, how their scores are interpreted, and how meaningful change is determined in follow-up.
In the previous lesson we saw that psychoacoustic measures do not show how much tinnitus bothers a person.
The impact of tinnitus on life is measured with standard scales that the person completes themselves.
One of the strongest recommendations of the American guideline is to tell bothersome tinnitus apart from tinnitus that is not bothersome.
Scales help make this distinction, set treatment goals, and monitor change.
The two most common scales are the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory and the Tinnitus Functional Index.

cumleler.yazi: The Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, or THI, was developed by Newman and colleagues in 1996.
cumleler.ses: The Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, or T H I, was developed by Newman and colleagues in nineteen ninety six.

cumleler.yazi: The THI has the same structure as the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, or DHI: 25 items and three answer options.
cumleler.ses: The T H I has the same structure as the Dizziness Handicap Inventory, or D H I: 25 items and three answer options.

cumleler: The functional subscale has 11 items about the impact on attention, sleep, work and social life.
The emotional subscale has 9 items about anger, anxiety, irritability and depressed feelings.
The catastrophic subscale has 5 items measuring despair, loss of control and the feeling of being unable to escape the tinnitus.
A yes answer scores 4, sometimes 2, and no 0; the total score ranges from 0 to 100.
In the clinic, interpretation usually relies on the total score rather than the subscales.

maddeler.metin: May be read aloud, but _not steered_

cumleler.yazi: The THI is a short scale, and most people complete it in a few minutes.
cumleler.ses: The T H I is a short scale, and most people complete it in a few minutes.

cumleler: The person is asked to answer the items thinking about the impact of their tinnitus today.
For people with reading difficulty, the items can be read in a neutral tone; the answers are not steered.
A blank item makes the total score look lower than it is, so the form is checked when it is handed in.
The scale reflects the perception of the person with tinnitus, not that of their family.
When the result is discussed with the patient, it becomes the starting point for counseling.

cumleler.yazi: A common grading of the THI total score is the five grades proposed by McCombe and colleagues in 2001.
cumleler.ses: A common grading of the T H I total score is the five grades proposed by McCombe and colleagues in two thousand one.

cumleler: A score of 0 to 16 is grade one, read as slight or no handicap.
A score of 18 to 36 is mild, and 38 to 56 is moderate handicap.
A score of 58 to 76 is defined as severe, and 78 to 100 as catastrophic.
Because each item scores 0, 2 or 4, the total is always an even number, so the cutoffs are even numbers too.
In this example, the score is 64 at baseline and falls to 38 six months later.
This means a move from the severe grade to the moderate grade.

maddeler.metin: Noticed by the patient: about 7 points
The two values answer different questions

cumleler: In follow-up, we need to decide whether the difference between two scores is a real change.
In Newman and colleagues' test-retest study, a difference of at least 20 points was needed for a statistically significant change.
A later study suggested that the clinical change a patient can notice may be smaller, about 7 points.
These two values answer different questions: one shows the limit of measurement error, the other the difference the patient feels.
The 26-point drop in our example is meaningful by both criteria.

cumleler.yazi: For users in Türkiye, a Turkish adaptation of the THI was published in 2007 and showed high internal consistency.
cumleler.ses: For users in Türkiye, a Turkish adaptation of the T H I was published in two thousand seven and showed high internal consistency.

cumleler.yazi: The Tinnitus Functional Index, or TFI, was published by Meikle and colleagues in 2012.
cumleler.ses: The Tinnitus Functional Index, or TFI, was published by Meikle and colleagues in twenty twelve.

cumleler: The TFI was developed both to measure the severity of impact and to be sensitive to change with treatment.
The scale has 25 items and eight subscales; most items are answered on a scale from 0 to 10.
The first subscale asks how intrusive the tinnitus is and how much it constantly grabs attention.
The second subscale measures how much control the person feels they have over their tinnitus.
The cognitive subscale asks about the impact on attention and thinking, and the sleep subscale about falling asleep and sleep duration.
The auditory subscale asks how much the tinnitus makes hearing and understanding speech harder.
The relaxation subscale measures the impact on resting and being able to stay calm.
The quality of life subscale asks about the impact on social activities, work and family life.
The emotional subscale assesses feelings of anxiety, sadness and distress.
Subscale scores guide counseling by showing which area the person struggles with most.
The TFI total score also ranges from 0 to 100; a higher score shows a bigger problem.
The total score is calculated by averaging the answered items and converting the result to a 0 to 100 scale.
By a common interpretation, a score below 25 shows a relatively mild problem.
A score of 25 to 50 is read as a significant problem that may call for intervention.
A score above 50 suggests a severe problem that may call for more intensive intervention.
According to the development study, a reduction of at least 13 points is an improvement the patient would find meaningful.
In this example the TFI score falls from 56 to 38; this 18-point drop is considered meaningful.
Both scales are valid and widely used; the choice depends on the purpose.

cumleler.yazi: The THI is short and easy to score, and because it has been used for many years, the literature has a lot of comparison data.
cumleler.ses: The T H I is short and easy to score, and because it has been used for many years, the literature has a lot of comparison data.

cumleler: Because a Turkish adaptation exists, it is widely used in clinics in Türkiye.
The TFI was designed to be more responsive to change with treatment, and its subscales are more detailed.
The NICE guideline recommends considering the TFI to assess the impact of tinnitus in adults.
Whichever scale is chosen, the same scale must always be used in following the same person.
If the TFI is to be used, first check whether a validated version exists in the patient's language, such as Turkish in Türkiye.
Scales are used at several points in the clinical workflow.
At the first visit, a baseline score is taken and bothersome tinnitus is identified.
Areas with high scores show the topics to address first in counseling.
After counseling or treatment, the scale is completed again, and the difference is compared with the criteria for meaningful change.
A scale does not make a diagnosis; a high score is a marker of how much the tinnitus affects the person.

sahneler.metin: Do not look only at the total score; read the catastrophic items. If you notice thoughts of self-harm, ask openly and refer without delay.
cumleler: A clinical tip: always review the scale once it is completed; do not look only at the total score.
Yes answers to the catastrophic items in particular can show that the person may be in serious distress.
If you notice hopelessness or thoughts of self-harm, ask about it openly and in a calm voice.
If there is such a risk, the person is referred to a mental health professional without delay.

maddeler.metin: Always the same scale in follow-up

cumleler.yazi: The THI has 25 items grouped into three subscales and is scored from 0 to 100.
cumleler.ses: The T H I has 25 items grouped into three subscales and is scored from 0 to 100.

cumleler.yazi: The THI score is interpreted in five grades; a difference of about 20 points is needed for statistically significant change.
cumleler.ses: The T H I score is interpreted in five grades; a difference of about 20 points is needed for statistically significant change.

cumleler: The TFI is a scale with eight subscales that is responsive to change; a reduction of at least 13 points counts as meaningful improvement.
The scale is chosen to fit the purpose, but the same scale is always used in following the same person.

sahneler.soru: What grade is a THI score of 46?
sahneler.aciklama: Scores from 38 to 56 are the _moderate_ grade.

cumleler.yazi: Test yourself: on the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, what grade is a person with a score of 46?

cumleler: The correct answer is B: moderate.
In the McCombe grading, scores between 38 and 56 are read as moderate handicap.
